name: New Haven
soil_note: Acidic, often sandy glacial till and coastal outwash; older urban lots near pre-1978 houses may carry lead, so test soil and use raised beds for food crops.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Hartford
soil_note: Connecticut River valley loams are fertile but often acidic; add lime per a soil test, and test older city yards for lead.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Boston
soil_note: Urban soils are often compacted fill with lead from old paint and traffic; test first and grow food in raised beds with clean compost-rich soil.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Worcester
soil_note: Rocky, acidic glacial till over hilly terrain; expect stones, add lime and compost, and choose a sunny slope to avoid frost pockets.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Springfield
soil_note: Pioneer Valley sandy loams drain well and warm early but are acidic and low in organic matter, so add compost yearly.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Cape Cod (Hyannis)
soil_note: Very sandy, acidic, fast-draining outwash soil; build organic matter with compost and mulch, and water deeply in summer.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Providence
soil_note: Acidic sandy loam and glacial till; urban and former industrial lots may contain lead, so test soil and use raised beds.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Burlington
soil_note: Champlain Valley soils range from heavy lake clay to sand; clay warms slowly in spring, so raised beds help early crops.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Concord
soil_note: Sandy, acidic Merrimack Valley soils drain fast and the valley is a frost pocket, so add compost and keep row cover handy into late May.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Portland
soil_note: Thin, rocky, acidic glacial soils; lime per a soil test and build raised beds with compost to warm the soil sooner.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Bangor
soil_note: Acidic glacial till and marine clays that stay cold and wet in spring; raised beds and dark mulch help warm-season crops.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Albany
soil_note: Hudson Valley soils include sandy pine-bush areas and heavy lake clays; check drainage and add compost either way.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: New York City
soil_note: City soils are frequently compacted fill that can contain lead and other contaminants; test soil and grow food in raised beds or containers.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Buffalo
soil_note: Heavy lake-plain clay loams drain slowly and stay cold in spring; raised beds and added organic matter improve drainage.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Syracuse
soil_note: Glacial till soils here are often less acidic (some limestone-derived); test pH before liming and add compost to heavier patches.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Newark
soil_note: Urban and former industrial soils can carry lead and other metals; test soil (Rutgers offers testing) and garden in raised beds.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Philadelphia
soil_note: Piedmont silt loams are productive, but older city lots often have lead from paint and fill; test soil before growing food in the ground.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)

name: Pittsburgh
soil_note: Hilly, clay-heavy soils over shale and sandstone drain slowly; add compost, and test older urban lots for lead.
source: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map 2023 (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov); NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Climate Normals; Old Farmer's Almanac frost dates (50%)
